reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it actively instructs viewers to join Forsage BUSD under an existing upline/team identifier and to connect and approve a wallet, presenting the flow alongside team and BUSD reward structures. The creator provides participation steps and offers help with difficulties, which promotes recruitment-dependent financial participation rather than neutrally demonstrating wallet connectivity.

opening.argument: The speaker does not promise income or present participation as profitable. Instead, the supplied narration expressly says “no money or any profit,” which is a material qualification against reading the walkthrough as a deceptive earnings pitch. The speaker also offers practical assistance if someone encounters difficulty, consistent with helping a user navigate a process rather than guaranteeing a financial result. The visible page shows zero team members and zero BUSD rewards, further weakening any claim that the video represents established returns.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats references to “our team” and an invitation as proof of recruitment-dependent financial participation, but those words do not establish promised commissions, earnings, or a guaranteed outcome. The displayed figures are Team 0 and Rewards, BUSD 0.00, which is inconsistent with presenting realized rewards. The wallet flow therefore remains compatible with a qualified walkthrough whose speaker expressly disclaims money or profit.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualification does not neutralize the operational solicitation. The narration still instructs the viewer to select BUSD, enter the speaker’s team, and start, while the interface identifies an upline and offers registration. Zero current rewards do not change the fact that the process is being directed toward participation; they only show the displayed account’s present balance.

opening.argument: The title frames the content as a how-to connection tutorial: “How to Connect Trust Wallet to Forsage.” The narration is procedural, describing opening the wallet, using the browser, pasting a link, and pressing Enter. The supplied frames likewise show browser navigation and a registration screen, including a visible “How to register in Forsage BUSD” section. These are concrete operational instructions, so the primary function can be understood as demonstrating a wallet and DApp workflow rather than making an evidentiary claim that the service is safe or profitable.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video a tutorial does not make it promotional. The title specifically describes connecting a wallet, and the narration focuses on navigation steps rather than a guarantee, testimonial, or earnings claim. The prosecution’s selected phrase about starting a team describes what appears during the demonstration, but it does not by itself establish that the creator is soliciting viewers for commissions.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The procedure is not a neutral wallet demonstration. It directs the viewer through Forsage BUSD registration, supplies an upline identifier, and tells the viewer to start the team. The page itself labels the flow “Registration in Forsage BUSD” and shows the upline field, so the tutorial framing does not erase its participation-directed purpose.

opening.argument: The supplied material does not show the core mechanics needed to establish a deceptive financial scheme. The visible page shows a registration interface with the wallet connected, but the sampled screen reports that the wallet is already registered and instructs the user to use another wallet or log in. The page also displays Team 0 and Rewards, BUSD 0.00. There is no supplied evidence of a completed payment, a guaranteed return, or a demonstrated downline payout. The narration even distinguishes the process from money or profit, making this more consistent with an operational service walkthrough than proof of a scam mechanism.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution can identify an upline field and an invitation, but those features alone do not prove a completed deposit, income promise, or payout. The supplied screen instead shows an already-registered-wallet error and zero displayed rewards. Describing a BUSD registration path is not the same as showing that viewers were deceived into transferring funds or receiving guaranteed returns.

citations.quote: i want my id no money or any profit

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The argument demands proof of completed harm when the relevant issue is promotion of the participation mechanism. The narration says to select BUSD, enter the team, and start, while the screen shows the upline identifier and registration stages including approval. The already-registered error is an incidental account state; it does not negate the instruction to use another wallet to register or log in.
